title: Young people still want stable work and homes, but the widening cultural shift is confidence in access rather than abandonment of traditional milestones
geography: 30 countries; global, generational, income and Western-country comparisons

denominator.unit: adults aged 16–74 across 30 countries, with country-specific age-frame variation

stable_full_time_job_marker.unit: percent viewing a stable full-time job as an important sign of a successful life

home_ownership_marker.unit: percent viewing owning a home as an important sign of a successful life

independent_living_marker.unit: percent viewing becoming independent and living on their own as important

parenthood_marker.unit: percent viewing becoming a parent as important

marriage_marker.unit: percent viewing marriage or civil partnership as important

observations.method: Ipsos Global Advisor survey asking respondents which milestones define a successful life.
observations.uncertainty: The global average is a simple country average, not population-weighted; aspiration importance is not the same as intended behavior, achievement or policy preference.
observations.subgroup: Adults aged 16–74 across 30 countries including the United States, Canada, Europe, Asia and Latin America.
observations.counterinterpretation: Stable work and home ownership may be selected as symbols of security rather than literal personal goals, especially where access is visibly constrained.

observations.period: 2026; confidence in reaching milestones by generation and income

denominator.unit: adults aged 16–74 across 30 countries; subgroup denominators are source-specific

generational_alignment.value: Under-35s, 35–49-year-olds and 50–74-year-olds place nearly the same importance on stable jobs and home ownership

income_opportunity_gradient.value: Higher-income households are more likely to regard milestones as important, have achieved them and feel confident achieving those outstanding

access_not_values_shift.value: Delayed adulthood appears more related to barriers to access and reduced confidence than to abandonment of traditional aspirations

observations.method: Comparative subgroup analysis of milestone importance, achievement and perceived attainability by generation and household income.
observations.uncertainty: The survey is cross-sectional and cannot separate age, cohort and life-stage effects or establish that income causes confidence in future attainment.
observations.subgroup: Gen Z, Millennials, Gen X and Baby Boomers, with higher- and lower-income household comparisons.
observations.counterinterpretation: Generational similarity in stated values may coexist with substantial differences in actual opportunity, debt, housing markets, family support and labor-market entry.

denominator.unit: adults aged 16–74 across 30 countries; source reports global average

sad_if_no_home_ownership.unit: percent saying they would feel sad if they never owned their own home

sad_if_no_stable_job.unit: percent saying they would feel sad if they never achieved a stable job

sad_if_no_own_living_space.unit: percent saying they would feel sad if they never lived in their own home, rented or owned

family_milestone_divergence.value: Parenthood and marriage produce more divided responses and are increasingly treated as personal choices rather than universal expectations

observations.method: Ipsos survey of emotional response to never achieving major work, housing, independence and family milestones.
observations.uncertainty: Hypothetical emotional responses do not measure distress, mental-health outcomes or actual life-course decisions.
observations.counterinterpretation: Sadness about an unmet milestone may reflect social status, security or lost optionality rather than a desire for the traditional institution itself.

observations.period: 2026; Western-country Gen Z expectations for pets and parenthood

denominator.unit: Gen Z respondents in Western countries; exact subgroup denominator not headlined on the public page

gen_z_pet_lifetime_expectation.unit: percent of Gen Z in Western countries who have owned an adult pet or expect to do so

gen_z_parenthood_lifetime_expectation.unit: percent of Gen Z in Western countries who have become or expect to become a parent

pet_parenthood_gap.unit: percentage-point difference between pet and parenthood expectation

consumer_life_stage_signal.value: Pet ownership can become a more attainable form of care, companionship and adult identity when parenthood and housing feel less accessible

observations.method: Ipsos comparison of Gen Z expectations for pet ownership and parenthood in Western countries.
observations.uncertainty: The comparison does not establish why expectations differ or whether pet ownership substitutes for parenthood; country, relationship, fertility, housing and income contexts matter.
observations.subgroup: Gen Z respondents in Western countries.
observations.counterinterpretation: Pet and parenthood expectations may be additive rather than substitutive, with the gap reflecting timing and uncertainty rather than a changed value hierarchy.

related_sources.claim: Ipsos iSay public explainer with global milestone rankings, sample and income-confidence interpretation.
Official Ipsos report-access page for the Life Aspirations 2026 study.

boundary: This record adds a life-course and consumer-culture mechanism: stable work and housing remain widely shared definitions of success, while income and access shape confidence, emotional stakes and the timing or substitution of family and care milestones. It is a cross-national public-opinion study, not a fertility forecast, housing-demand model, longitudinal life-course panel or proof that pet ownership replaces parenthood.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: The official Ipsos UK article, Ipsos iSay explainer and report-access page were retrieved and reviewed for sample, milestone rankings, generational alignment, income opportunity gradient, emotional cost of unmet milestones and Gen Z pet/parenthood expectations; the accessible official article page was hashed because the full report download is gated behind registration.
